1.5 Separating Floor Effect






Important



Luckily, Muthen et al. actually came out with a pretty clever and theoretically meaningful way to address floor effects: a hurdle modeling approach.
Instead of dropping the floor effect (the lowest value possible), Muthen et al. recommends creating two variables from the original variable.
Step 1: Create a binary variable.
Create a binary variable that collapses all non-floor scores as 1. Thus, conceptually this variable represents whether a construct is meaingfully occuring or not.
BIN = 0, the construct is not meaningfully occuring. BIN = 1, the construct is meaningfully occuring.
We do loose information about the magnitude of how this construct is taking place, but that’s where part 2 comes in.
Step 2: Create a continuous variable.
In the second step, we code all floor effects as NA (i.e., missing) and retain non-floor effects as original.
Thus, the continous variable is represents what is taking place AFTER removed floor effects which drowned out the variance.
Thus, in analytical models we should include both variables (only possible in SEMs) and allowed to correlate with one another. In doing so, we can understand if a distal variable is related to the occurrence of a construct AND also when it is occurring, the magnitude of that relationship.
For the truncated variable, we will use a tobit/censored specification.

2.2.2 Model Specification

pos_ctsem <- "
# Cross-level interaction declarations -- which TIpreds exist, and (inline
# below) which DRIFT parameter(s) each one is allowed to moderate. Only
# posaff_W (the within-person factor) gets TIpred moderation here --
# posaff_B (the between-person factor) is left unrestricted/untouched, same
# as before.
TIPRED: zpos, zneg, zdis

# Measurement Model
posaff_B =~ esm_pa
posaff_W =~ esm_pa

# Between/Trend
posaff_B  ~  0*posaff_B     
posaff_B ~~  0*posaff_B # this is what tells model its between-person
posaff_B %~% posaff_B     

# Within (dynamic) factor
posaff_W  ~  posaff_W + posaff_W:zpos + posaff_W:zneg + posaff_W:zdis
posaff_W ~~  posaff_W       
posaff_W %~% posaff_W       

# CINT
posaff_B ~ 0
"

Note



The first parameter represents the overall between-person detrend of Positive Affect (0), which we set as a latent random intercept that capture the stable trait.
The second parameter represents the within-person dynamic return of PA to equilibrium (-3.703 [-4.976, -2.581]). What does this mean practically? This tells us how fast a process returns to equilibrium.
We can actually calculate the half-life using the following:

Note

3.2.1 Model Specification

psx_sum_ctsem <- "
# Measurement Model
psx_B =~ esm_psx_sum
psx_W =~ esm_psx_sum

# Between/Trend
psx_B  ~  psx_B
psx_B ~~  0*psx_B

# Within (dynamic) factor

psx_W ~~  psx_W

## T0MEAN

CENSOR: esm_psx_sum
"

psx_censored_mod <- ctModel(
  type          = "ct",
  id            = "id",
  time          = "time_day",
  latentNames   = psx_censored_syn$latentNames,
  manifestNames = psx_censored_syn$manifestNames,
  LAMBDA        = psx_censored_syn$LAMBDA,
  DRIFT         = psx_censored_syn$DRIFT,
  DIFFUSION     = psx_censored_syn$DIFFUSION,
  T0VAR         = psx_censored_syn$T0VAR,
  CINT          = psx_censored_syn$CINT,
  T0MEANS       = psx_censored_syn$T0MEANS,
  MANIFESTMEANS = psx_censored_syn$MANIFESTMEANS,
  manifesttype  = psx_censored_syn$manifesttype,
  censormin     = psx_censored_syn$censormin,
  censormax     = psx_censored_syn$censormax,
  n.TIpred      = 3,
  TIpredNames   = c("zpos", "zneg", "zdis")
)

effect_cols <- c("zpos_effect", "zneg_effect", "zdis_effect")

# Reverted per request: apply TIpred moderation to every parameter (both
# the between/trait psx_B and within/dynamic psx_W processes), matching
# ctModel()'s own default (tipredDefault = TRUE leaves every cell's effect
# columns TRUE already) rather than restricting to psx_W only. No blanket
# off/selective re-enable here anymore -- this block just confirms/leaves
# the default in place and prints it for visibility.
psx_w_idx <- match("psx_W", psx_censored_syn$latentNames)
target_psx_w <- psx_censored_mod$pars$matrix == "DRIFT" &
  as.character(psx_censored_mod$pars$row) == as.character(psx_w_idx) &
  as.character(psx_censored_mod$pars$col) == as.character(psx_w_idx)

# Safety check: ctModel() has been observed to silently default
# indvarying = FALSE on a free DRIFT diagonal parameter even when nothing
# in this script asked for that. Confirm psx_W's autoregression is still
# individually varying, and force it back on if ctModel() defaulted it off.
stopifnot("indvarying" %in% names(psx_censored_mod$pars))

3.3 Two-Part Approach (Censored Magnitude)

3.3.1 Model Specification

psx_twopart_ctsem <- "

TIPRED: zpos, zneg, zdis
# Measurement Model
## BINARY
bin_psx_B =~ esm_psx_bin
bin_psx_W =~ esm_psx_bin

## CONT.
con_psx_B =~ esm_psx_con
con_psx_W =~ esm_psx_con

# Between/Trend
bin_psx_B  ~  0*bin_psx_B
bin_psx_B ~~  0*bin_psx_B
bin_psx_B %~% bin_psx_B

con_psx_B  ~  0*con_psx_B
con_psx_B ~~  0*con_psx_B
con_psx_B %~% con_psx_B

bin_psx_B %~% con_psx_B

# Within (dynamic) factor
## BINARY
bin_psx_W  ~  bin_psx_W + bin_psx_W:zpos + bin_psx_W:zneg + bin_psx_W:zdis
bin_psx_W ~~  bin_psx_W
bin_psx_W %~% bin_psx_W

## CONT.
con_psx_W  ~  con_psx_W + con_psx_W:zpos + con_psx_W:zneg + con_psx_W:zdis
con_psx_W ~~  con_psx_W
con_psx_W %~% con_psx_W

## T0MEAN
bin_psx_B ~t0~ 1
con_psx_B ~t0~ 1

# esm_psx_con ~ 1

BINARY: esm_psx_bin
CENSOR: esm_psx_con
"

Technical interpretation: when an individual reports PSX, the elevated likelihood of reporting PSX again decays at a specific rate (−3.482) — i.e., endorsing PSX at one moment tells you little about whether they’ll endorse it again shortly after; occurrence is not “sticky.”

Technical interpretation: when someone reports greater PSX, that elevated severity tends to persist — it takes longer to decay back down to their typical (floor) level, rather than resolving quickly.
Putting them together: occurrence is volatile (endorsing PSX at any moment doesn’t predict endorsing it again soon), while magnitude is inertial (once severity rises, it stays elevated for a while before subsiding) — i.e., whether someone reports PSX fluctuates quickly, but how bad it is when they do tends to linger.

TIPRED: zpos, zneg, zdis

## BINARY
bin_na_B =~ esm_na_bin
bin_na_W =~ esm_na_bin

## CONT.
con_na_B =~ esm_na_con
con_na_W =~ esm_na_con

# Between

bin_na_B ~~  0*bin_na_B
bin_na_B %~% bin_na_B

con_na_B  ~  0*con_na_B
con_na_B ~~  0*con_na_B
con_na_B %~% con_na_B

bin_na_B %~% con_na_B

# Within (dynamic) factor
## BINARY
bin_na_W  ~  bin_na_W
bin_na_W ~~  bin_na_W
bin_na_W %~% bin_na_W

## CONT.
con_na_W  ~  con_na_W
con_na_W ~~  con_na_W
con_na_W %~% con_na_W

## T0MEAN
bin_na_B ~t0~ 1
con_na_B ~t0~ 1

BINARY: esm_na_bin
CENSOR: esm_na_con

# Measurement Model
## BINARY
bin_dis_B =~ esm_dis_bin
bin_dis_W =~ esm_dis_bin

## CONT.
con_dis_B =~ esm_dis_con
con_dis_W =~ esm_dis_con

# Between
bin_dis_B  ~  0*bin_dis_B
bin_dis_B ~~  0*bin_dis_B
bin_dis_B %~% bin_dis_B

con_dis_B  ~  0*con_dis_B
con_dis_B ~~  0*con_dis_B
con_dis_B %~% con_dis_B

bin_dis_B %~% con_dis_B

# Within (dynamic) factor
## BINARY
bin_dis_W  ~  bin_dis_W
bin_dis_W ~~  bin_dis_W
bin_dis_W %~% bin_dis_W

## CONT.
con_dis_W  ~  con_dis_W
con_dis_W ~~  con_dis_W
con_dis_W %~% con_dis_W

## T0MEAN
bin_dis_B ~t0~ 1
con_dis_B ~t0~ 1

BINARY: esm_dis_bin
CENSOR: esm_dis_con
"

dis_twopart_syn <- ct_lavaan(dis_twopart_ctsem, data = p5_data)

dis_twopart_mod <- ctModel(
  type          = "ct",
  id            = "id",
  time          = "time_day",
  latentNames   = dis_twopart_syn$latentNames,
  manifestNames = dis_twopart_syn$manifestNames,
  LAMBDA        = dis_twopart_syn$LAMBDA,
  DRIFT         = dis_twopart_syn$DRIFT,
  DIFFUSION     = dis_twopart_syn$DIFFUSION,
  T0VAR         = dis_twopart_syn$T0VAR,
  CINT          = dis_twopart_syn$CINT,
  T0MEANS       = dis_twopart_syn$T0MEANS,
  MANIFESTMEANS = dis_twopart_syn$MANIFESTMEANS,
  manifesttype  = dis_twopart_syn$manifesttype,
  censormin     = dis_twopart_syn$censormin,
  censormax     = dis_twopart_syn$censormax,
  n.TIpred      = 3,
  TIpredNames   = c("zpos", "zneg", "zdis")
)

effect_cols <- c("zpos_effect", "zneg_effect", "zdis_effect")

# Only interested in cross-level moderation of the within-person (dynamic)
# processes' autoregression -- not the between-person/trait processes, and
# not any of the bin<->con cross-latent DRIFT paths (never specified in
# this spec, fixed at 0 by default, but ctModel() still defaults their
# TIpred effects to TRUE regardless of that fixed value). Start by
# switching every parameter's TIpred effects off, then re-enable only the
# two within-person autoregressions.
dis_twopart_mod$pars[, effect_cols] <- FALSE

bin_w_idx <- match("bin_dis_W", dis_twopart_syn$latentNames)
con_w_idx <- match("con_dis_W", dis_twopart_syn$latentNames)

target_bin_w <- dis_twopart_mod$pars$matrix == "DRIFT" &
  as.character(dis_twopart_mod$pars$row) == as.character(bin_w_idx) &
  as.character(dis_twopart_mod$pars$col) == as.character(bin_w_idx)
target_con_w <- dis_twopart_mod$pars$matrix == "DRIFT" &
  as.character(dis_twopart_mod$pars$row) == as.character(con_w_idx) &
  as.character(dis_twopart_mod$pars$col) == as.character(con_w_idx)

dis_twopart_mod$pars[target_bin_w | target_con_w, effect_cols] <- TRUE


stopifnot("indvarying" %in% names(dis_twopart_mod$pars))
dis_twopart_mod$pars[target_bin_w | target_con_w, "indvarying"] <- TRUE

print(dis_twopart_mod$pars[dis_twopart_mod$pars$matrix == "DRIFT",
                           c("matrix", "row", "col", "indvarying", effect_cols)])

6.2 Two-Part Approach (Censored Magnitude)

6.2.1 Model Specification

neg3_twopart_ctsem <- "
# Measurement Model
## BINARY
bin_neg3_B =~ esm_neg3_bin
bin_neg3_W =~ esm_neg3_bin

## CONT.
con_neg3_B =~ esm_neg3_con
con_neg3_W =~ esm_neg3_con

# Between/Trend
bin_neg3_B  ~  0*bin_neg3_B
bin_neg3_B ~~  0*bin_neg3_B
bin_neg3_B %~% bin_neg3_B

con_neg3_B  ~  0*con_neg3_B
con_neg3_B ~~  0*con_neg3_B
con_neg3_B %~% con_neg3_B

bin_neg3_B %~% con_neg3_B

# Within (dynamic) factor
## BINARY
bin_neg3_W  ~  bin_neg3_W
bin_neg3_W ~~  bin_neg3_W
bin_neg3_W %~% bin_neg3_W

## CONT.
con_neg3_W  ~  con_neg3_W
con_neg3_W ~~  con_neg3_W
con_neg3_W %~% con_neg3_W

## T0MEAN
bin_neg3_B ~t0~ 1
con_neg3_B ~t0~ 1

BINARY: esm_neg3_bin
CENSOR: esm_neg3_con
"

neg3_twopart_syn <- ct_lavaan(neg3_twopart_ctsem, data = p6_data)

neg3_twopart_mod <- ctModel(
  type          = "ct",
  id            = "id",
  time          = "time_day",
  latentNames   = neg3_twopart_syn$latentNames,
  manifestNames = neg3_twopart_syn$manifestNames,
  LAMBDA        = neg3_twopart_syn$LAMBDA,
  DRIFT         = neg3_twopart_syn$DRIFT,
  DIFFUSION     = neg3_twopart_syn$DIFFUSION,
  T0VAR         = neg3_twopart_syn$T0VAR,
  CINT          = neg3_twopart_syn$CINT,
  T0MEANS       = neg3_twopart_syn$T0MEANS,
  MANIFESTMEANS = neg3_twopart_syn$MANIFESTMEANS,
  manifesttype  = neg3_twopart_syn$manifesttype,
  censormin     = neg3_twopart_syn$censormin,
  censormax     = neg3_twopart_syn$censormax,
  n.TIpred      = 3,
  TIpredNames   = c("zpos", "zneg", "zdis")
)

effect_cols <- c("zpos_effect", "zneg_effect", "zdis_effect")

# Only interested in cross-level moderation of the within-person (dynamic)
# processes' autoregression -- not the between-person/trait processes, and
# not any of the bin<->con cross-latent DRIFT paths (never specified in
# this spec, fixed at 0 by default, but ctModel() still defaults their
# TIpred effects to TRUE regardless of that fixed value). Start by
# switching every parameter's TIpred effects off, then re-enable only the
# two within-person autoregressions.
neg3_twopart_mod$pars[, effect_cols] <- FALSE

bin_w_idx <- match("bin_neg3_W", neg3_twopart_syn$latentNames)
con_w_idx <- match("con_neg3_W", neg3_twopart_syn$latentNames)

target_bin_w <- neg3_twopart_mod$pars$matrix == "DRIFT" &
  as.character(neg3_twopart_mod$pars$row) == as.character(bin_w_idx) &
  as.character(neg3_twopart_mod$pars$col) == as.character(bin_w_idx)
target_con_w <- neg3_twopart_mod$pars$matrix == "DRIFT" &
  as.character(neg3_twopart_mod$pars$row) == as.character(con_w_idx) &
  as.character(neg3_twopart_mod$pars$col) == as.character(con_w_idx)

neg3_twopart_mod$pars[target_bin_w | target_con_w, effect_cols] <- TRUE

# Safety check: ctModel() has been observed to silently default
# indvarying = FALSE on a free DRIFT diagonal parameter (found with
# con_psx_W in 03_ple_model.qmd) even when nothing in this script asked
# for that. Confirm both within-person autoregressions are still
# individually varying, and force them back on if ctModel() defaulted
# either off.
stopifnot("indvarying" %in% names(neg3_twopart_mod$pars))
neg3_twopart_mod$pars[target_bin_w | target_con_w, "indvarying"] <- TRUE

print(neg3_twopart_mod$pars[neg3_twopart_mod$pars$matrix == "DRIFT",
